zh.title: 雪梨西部新機場耗資140億啟用 首班捷星航班起飛
zh.summary: 西部機場啟用；首班捷星航班售罄起飛；免宵禁、貨運服務同步上線
body: 雪梨西部新機場耗資 140 億澳元正式啟用，成為該地區首座免宵禁的大型航空樞紐。
首班捷星航班已售罄並順利起飛，標誌商業客運服務正式投入營運。
機場同步啟動貨運服務，提供全天候國際物流運輸能力。
官方表示免宵禁設計與客貨並運模式將大幅提升雪梨整體航空運力。
這座新機場的開幕儀式包含首班捷星客機起飛與首航貨機升空，彰顯雙重功能定位。

en.title: Western Sydney's new $14 billion airport opens as first Jetstar flight departs
en.summary: Western Sydney Airport opens; first Jetstar flight sold out; curfew‑free hub launches freight services
body: The newly opened Western Sydney airport, built at a cost of fourteen billion Australian dollars, officially began operations today as the region’s first curfew‑free major aviation hub.
The inaugural Jetstar flight departed fully booked, signalling the launch of scheduled passenger services from the new facility.
At the same time, freight services were activated, giving the airport round‑the‑clock international logistics capability.
Officials said the airport’s curfew‑free design and combined passenger and cargo operations will boost Sydney’s overall air transport capacity.
The opening ceremony featured the first Jetstar departure and the inaugural cargo flight, underscoring the hub’s dual‑role mission.

zh.title: A350-1000 獲青睞 空中巴士十年期盼成真
zh.summary: A350-1000 受青睞；波音 777X 進度落後
body: Simple Flying 指出，空中巴士 A350-1000 正獲得航空公司青睞，這是十年前空中巴士所期盼的局面。
報導並提到，隨著波音 777X 進度進一步落後，長程市場競爭格局正在改變。
根據早先資料，漢莎航空已選定東京作為其首架 A350-1000 商業首航目的地，計劃於 2026 年 12 月 3 日從慕尼黑起飛。
波音近期第三季僅交付五架 777 型機，顯示 777X 計劃仍面臨交付壓力。

en.title: A350-1000 gains popularity Airbus hoped for a decade ago as 777X slips further
en.summary: A350-1000 gains airline favor; Boeing 777X schedule slips further
body: Simple Flying notes that the Airbus A350-1000 is gaining the popularity the manufacturer hoped for a decade ago.
The article adds that the aircraft is gaining ground as Boeing’s 777X slips further behind schedule, reshaping the battle for long‑haul dominance.
Earlier records show Lufthansa has selected Tokyo as the launch destination for its first A350‑1000 commercial flight, slated to depart Munich on 3 December 2026.
Boeing’s third‑quarter deliveries included only five 777‑type aircraft, underscoring continued delivery pressure on the 777X programme.
